evals.prompt: Where in the Rain docs is settlement for partner-managed programs explained? Give me the link.
evals.expected_output: Routes to rain-docs-search. Runs search_docs.sh against the Mintlify Search API (assistant key + domain slug from env), de-duplicates results by path, and returns a verified https://docs.rain.xyz/... link, noting the Rain-Managed vs Partner-Managed variant. Does NOT guess a URL from memory.

evals.prompt: A client asked how to activate a physical Rain card — find the right docs page to link in my reply.
evals.expected_output: Routes to rain-docs-search. Searches with short keyword queries (e.g. "physical card activation"), presents the page title + docs.rain.xyz link + one-line reason. May quote the matched content chunk. Does not attempt to perform the activation via the Rain API.

evals.prompt: Pull our docs usage stats from Mintlify for this quarter — top searches, page views, unique visitors, and assistant queries — like the numbers in the Coinbase case study.
evals.expected_output: Routes to rain-docs-search. Uses docs_analytics.sh with the admin key and projectId, passes explicit dateFrom/dateTo, pages through limit/offset/hasMore before totalling, and presents the numbers grouped as discoverability / AI engagement / content quality with the date range stated.

evals.prompt: Ask the Rain docs assistant what the difference between Rain-Managed and Partner-Managed authorization is, and cite the source pages.
evals.expected_output: Routes to rain-docs-search. Uses ask_assistant.sh (streamed response), relays the grounded answer and cites the retrieved page paths as docs.rain.xyz links.

evals.prompt: Get the credit balance for a Rain user.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT use rain-docs-search. Routes to rain-api-generic (calling a raincards.xyz endpoint, not finding documentation).

evals.prompt: My Rain API call returns 401 — how do I fix authentication?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT use rain-docs-search. Routes to rain-api-auth (Api-Key header and 401/403 triage live there). rain-docs-search would only assist if the user explicitly asked to find the docs page covering it.
